chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most by which my community will enter Paradise is God-consciousness and good character.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two main qualities that lead to entering Paradise according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identifies taqwa and husn al-khuluq as the most frequent causes for his ummah's entry into Paradise, highlighting the inseparable link between inner piety and outward ethical conduct. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on moral refinement as a practical manifestation of faith, serving as a key criterion for divine acceptance in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most by which my<sup>saww</sup> community would be entering the Paradise is fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and good manners’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The fact for which most people from my followers will go to paradise are piety before Allah and excellence in moral behavior.’”
